skill.name: agent-ui
skill.description: Guidance for adding the inference.sh Agent component to React and Next.js applications. It covers installation, proxy setup, environment configuration, streaming UI, approvals, widgets, and browser tools.
skill.summary: Add a React or Next.js agent interface with streaming, approvals, widgets, and scoped browser tools.
skill.author: inference-sh

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences, inline property names, and documentation links. One low-severity supply-chain concern remains because the quick start asks users to fetch a component from a remote registry URL. No prompt injection, secret exfiltration, or malicious intent was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Remote component installation from a URL
remediation.suggestion: Pin the registry artifact or release, and tell users to inspect downloaded component changes before installing.

remediation.issue: API key setup needs clearer handling
remediation.suggestion: State that INFERENCE_API_KEY must stay server-side, remain out of source control, and be rotated after exposure.

content.value_statement: Agent interfaces require streaming chat, tool states, approvals, and runtime wiring. This skill helps add a React or Next.js agent component with proxy setup, scoped tools, and UI patterns.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the agent block with shadcn and the inference.sh registry URL.
Defines a Next.js proxy route using the inference.sh SDK.
Documents the INFERENCE_API_KEY environment variable needed for the proxy.
Demonstrates Agent usage with proxy URL, model reference, description, and system prompt settings.
Shows scoped browser tools for form scanning and field filling.
Links to agent, SDK, human review, and generative UI documentation.
limitations: It is documentation only; it does not include the actual component source.
It depends on inference.sh services, SDK packages, and remote registry availability.
Users must manage API keys and proxy route security in their own application.
The examples target React and Next.js, not other frontend frameworks.

best_practices: Keep API keys only in server-side environment files and never expose them to browser code.
Use explicit approval states before tools change user data or submit forms.
Review remote component changes before installing them into a production repository.
anti_patterns: Do not place API keys in client components or public environment variables.
Do not enable file or image uploads without size, type, and retention rules.
Do not let browser tools update forms without visible user approval.

faq.question: What does this skill help build?
faq.answer: It helps build React and Next.js agent interfaces with streaming, approvals, widgets, and browser tool patterns.

faq.question: Does it include backend logic?
faq.answer: It points to an inference.sh SDK proxy route, but application teams still own deployment and security.

faq.question: Does it require an API key?
faq.answer: Yes. The setup example shows INFERENCE_API_KEY as a required server-side environment value.

faq.question: Can it support human approval flows?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented features include pending states, progress states, approval flows, and tool results.

faq.question: Can it fill forms in the browser?
faq.answer: The skill shows scoped client-side tools for scanning form fields and filling values through the agent.

faq.question: Is it specific to inference.sh?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples use inference.sh registry assets, SDK routes, services, and documentation.
